newsitem.title: CONGO: Shooting reported near Brazzaville presidency.
newsitem.headline: Shooting reported near Brazzaville presidency.

text.p: Shooting broke out on Friday near the presidency in the capital of Congo Brazzaville after a second day of gunfights between supporters of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso and the army, witnesses said.

The shooting began after the start of a second night of curfew in Brazzaville, where the government of Pascal Lissouba has ordered a crackdown on private militias and unauthorised possession of weapons, they added.
The significance of the shooting near the presidency was not immediately clear.
One witness spoke of a rocket-propelled grenade or a mortar shell exploding in the grounds of the presidency.

Residents said the national radio and television had stopped broadcasting. International telephone links with the former French colony were down. Contacts were possible via the mobile telephone network in Laurent Kabila Democratic Republic of Congo to the south.

The showdown between Sassou Nguesso and the army follows bloody clashes in the north of the country between supporters of the former president and of Lissouba's campaign manager. The clashes have resulted in the deaths of 16 people in less than a month.
